prompt:
Feature: let operators give yt-dlp a cookies file for video imports.

Video imports (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram) download the audio with yt-dlp. Some platforms refuse anonymous downloads (age-restricted or login-only videos, bot checks), and yt-dlp's standard answer is a Netscape-format cookies file, passed as its cookiefile option. Mealie has no way to hand one over.

Expected:
- A new setting YTDLP_COOKIEFILE on AppSettings, read from the environment like the other settings: an optional string, default None. Document it with the other backend settings as the path of a cookies file for yt-dlp.
- The transcription module, mealie.services.openai.transcription (the one with download_video(url, temp_path)), reads the setting through get_app_settings, imported into that module by name and called when a download starts, not at import time. The tests swap mealie.services.openai.transcription.get_app_settings for a stub returning an object whose only attribute is YTDLP_COOKIEFILE, and swap yt_dlp.YoutubeDL for a fake that records the options dict it was constructed with.
- When the setting is unset (None), the options dict passed to yt_dlp.YoutubeDL has no cookiefile key at all and the download runs exactly as today.
- When it is set, download_video passes the configured value as the cookiefile option, as the string it was given (YTDLP_COOKIEFILE="/data/cookies.txt" gives ydl_opts["cookiefile"] == "/data/cookies.txt"). The other options (format, output template, subtitles, post-processing) are unchanged.
- The value is used for downloads only; it is not reported by the app or admin about endpoints.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/services_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
title: feat: allow user to specify cookiefile for yt-dlp (#7363)
